title: ToolGuard step1 per-tool guard spec
description: Shape of one <tool_name>.json file under a benchmark's ground_truth/step1/ directory. Derived from the 26 employee-benchmark specs. Every spec belongs to exactly one real tool: there is no cross-tool 'global' spec, so a rule with no tool to attach to is simply absent, and orphan guidance is detected by finding policy-document text that no reference quotes. A spec carries only enforceable content: tool metadata lives in inputs/tool_enrichment.json, and a rule that was considered and rejected leaves no trace beyond the absence of the rule (or, for a wholly unconstrained tool, the absence of the spec file).

tool_name.description: Name of the guarded tool. Must equal the file's basename without .json.

source_doc.description: Path to the policy document the references are quoted from.

policy_items.description: Active guard rules for this tool, ANDed together at enforcement time. May be empty when every candidate rule was archived.

conflicts.description: Open (unresolved) interactions between two or more of this tool's policy_items. A conflict exists only while it is pending: once decided, the entry is removed and the decision is recorded on the affected policy_items' resolved_by_user. Omitted entirely when there are none.

id.description: Stable rule id, conventionally '<tool_name>.<rule_slug>'. Unique within the file (and, in practice, across the benchmark).

description.description: Full enforceable statement of the rule, including the deny condition and any not-applicable cases.

references.description: Verbatim quotes from source_doc that justify the rule. All 91 references in the employee specs are exact substrings of the policy document, so exact-quote is the intended contract.

trigger.description: 'pre_tool' evaluates before the call and can deny it; 'post_tool' evaluates after and describes a required side effect or result filtering.

skip.description: Excludes the rule from reference scoring. Absent (i.e. false) throughout the ground truth; declared because the eval filters on it and generated specs emit it on every item.

pending_for_user.description: Open questions that block full enforcement of this rule. Mutually exclusive with resolved_by_user in the observed data.

resolved_by_user.description: Questions that were raised and answered; the answer is baked into this rule.

requires.description: The context a guard needs in order to evaluate this rule. All three keys are always present, and 'nothing needed' is always the empty/false value — never null.

system_vars.description: Names of caller-context variables the rule reads. Must be declared in the benchmark's inputs/system_vars.json. Empty array means none needed.

tool_history.description: Prior read-only tool calls whose results the rule depends on. Empty array means none needed.

message_history.description: True when the rule must inspect the conversation (e.g. to find an explicit user 'yes'); false when it need not.

tool.description: Name of the tool that must have been called.

params.description: Argument bindings for that call, as parameter name -> expression over the guarded call. Observed expression forms: 'input.arguments.<field>', 'input.extensions.subject.<field>', and the function call 'year-of(input.arguments.<field>)'.

pendingQuestion.description: An unanswered question for the policy owner.

resolvedQuestion.description: A question that has been answered.

type.description: 'clarification' = the policy document is ambiguous; 'missing_variable' = a needed signal is not in system_vars; 'missing_tool' = a needed tool does not exist.

question.description: The question posed to the policy owner.

suggested_source.description: Where the missing signal could come from. Required when type is 'missing_variable', forbidden otherwise.

suggested_tool.description: Tool that would need to exist. Required when type is 'missing_tool', forbidden otherwise.

decided_by.description: Who decided. Only 'human' occurs in the observed data.

effect.description: What changed in the spec as a result.

kind.description: Conflict category: 'scope' = unclear which callers a rule binds; 'definition' = a term the rules share is undefined.

conflicting_policies.description: Ids of the policy_items that interact. Must resolve to ids in this file's policy_items — a conflict spanning several tools is recorded once per affected tool, each copy scoped to that tool's own items and correlated by a shared id slug.

description.description: When the conflict applies and why it is ambiguous.

question.description: The question that would settle it.

resolution.description: Always null: a conflict entry only exists while pending. A resolved conflict is deleted from this array and its decision recorded as a resolved_by_user entry on the affected policy_items.
